advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert git ls-files ran successfully and returned a non-empty tracked-file list before trusting an empty offenders result in test_guard_no_real_pat_in_tracked_tree.
evidence: `tracked = _git(["ls-files"]).stdout.splitlines()`
`_git` runs with `check=False` (line ~62), so a non-zero git exit yields empty stdout with no error surfaced
`for rel in tracked:` then `assert not offenders` — empty `tracked` means the assertion passes without scanning anything
This is the primary security-guard oracle (AC #1); its negative result must mean 'scanned and clean', not 'never scanned'
advisory.finding: test_guard_no_real_pat_in_tracked_tree fails open: it iterates over `_git(["ls-files"]).stdout.splitlines()` with check=False, so if git fails or returns an empty list the for-loop body never runs and the `assert not offenders` passes vacuously — a broken/empty git invocation is indistinguishable from a genuinely clean tree, defeating the committed-secret guard.
scenarios: Test invoked outside a git checkout, or git ls-files errors (returncode!=0)
CI environment where the repo is exported without .git
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `res.returncode == 0` on the ls-files call and `assert tracked, "git ls-files returned no tracked files — guard did not run"` before the scan loop.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm PAT values are constrained to single-line opaque tokens (or quote/validate them) before writing to the .env.
evidence: `echo "MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT=${mcp_pat_copilot}"`
Values come from SSM SecureStrings whose content is operator-supplied and not validated to be a single-line opaque token
This mirrors the existing precedent for other secrets in the same heredoc, so risk is bounded, but the PAT is a new operator-seeded value with no format constraint
advisory.finding: The raw PAT is written to the .env via `echo "MCP_CLIENT_PAT_COPILOT=${mcp_pat_copilot}"` with no quoting/escaping; a PAT containing whitespace, `#`, or newlines would corrupt the .env line or leak into adjacent values when the .env is sourced/parsed by compose.
scenarios: Operator seeds an SSM SecureString value containing a newline or shell/.env-significant character

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the rebar-mcp compose service (or wire an existing consumer) to bind-mount infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json into the container at the mcp.auth_static_tokens_file path and pass MCP_CLIENT_PAT_* via env_file, so the materialized tokens are actually reachable by the verifier.
evidence: search_files 'mcp' in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml returned (no matches); search_files 'auth_static_tokens_file' has NO match under infra/compose
search_files 'rebar-mcp' in infra/compose returned (no matches)
docker-compose.yml services block (lines 25-120) contains only 'gerrit' and 'review-bot' — no MCP service

docker-compose.yml:121-125 documents the same class of bug (beb1): 'that path does not exist in this container's namespace, so rebar silently wrote every event unsigned' — a HOST-materialized artifact needs an explicit mount/env override to reach the container
fetch-secrets.sh:160 writes mcp-static-tokens.json next to .env on the host with no compose bind-mount added in this change
advisory.finding: The materialized mcp-static-tokens.json and MCP_CLIENT_PAT_* env vars have no consumer: docker-compose.yml declares no rebar-mcp service, no bind-mount of the tokens file into a container, and no wiring of mcp.auth_static_tokens_file / the MCP_CLIENT_PAT_* env vars. The verifier (which reads mcp.auth_static_tokens_file at init and resolves token_env from its own process env) can never see the host-materialized file or the env vars.
scenarios: Operator seeds a PAT, re-materializes, and restarts rebar-mcp expecting auth to work, but the container's mcp.auth_static_tokens_file resolves to a path absent from the container filesystem (or the MCP_CLIENT_PAT_* env is unset in the container), so the token set is empty and all clients are rejected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add '--exclude infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json.*' (matching the .gitignore glob) to autodeploy RSYNC_EXCLUDES so interrupted-materialize temp files are protected like the .env/tokens precedent.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:165-166 RSYNC_EXCLUDES lists only '--exclude infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json' (no glob for the temp files)
.gitignore:99 'infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json.*' shows the temp files are recognized as artifacts
fetch-secrets.sh:174 'mcp_tokens_tmp="$(mktemp "${mcp_static_tokens_path}.XXXXXX")"' creates .XXXXXX temp files in the same dir
advisory.finding: The mcp-static-tokens.json.* mktemp temp files are gitignored but NOT added to autodeploy RSYNC_EXCLUDES; only the exact 'infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json' is excluded. A materialize interrupted between mktemp and mv can leave a temp file that rsync will then propagate/manage (and rsync --delete semantics differ from the protected canonical file).
scenarios: fetch-secrets.sh is killed after mktemp but before mv (OOM, reboot); a mcp-static-tokens.json.abc123 (0600, containing a written token set) survives in infra/compose and is not excluded from the deploy rsync.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `--exclude 'infra/compose/mcp-static-tokens.json.*'` to the RSYNC_EXCLUDES array in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that constructs StaticBearerVerifier / calls _load_static_tokens on the all-blank materialized {"tokens": []} file and asserts it raises AuthConfigError (fail-closed).
evidence: Runbook contract (added): infra/runbooks/mcp-client-pats.md — 'When all slots are blank the file is {"tokens": []} and the static verifier fails-closed at startup ("defines no tokens") until an operator populates at least one PAT.'
Production path: src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:724-725 'if not by_digest: raise AuthConfigError(f"static tokens file {tokens_file!r} defines no tokens")'

Test asserts only structure: tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py:236 'assert json.loads(tokens_file2.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["tokens"] == []' with no call to _load_static_tokens/StaticBearerVerifier on the empty file.
Named violating input: the all-blank materialized file {"tokens": []} — the diff adds its emission but no test drives the verifier over it to confirm the fail-closed AuthConfigError.
advisory.finding: The all-blank fail-closed contract is asserted only at the file-content level, never through the verifier. test_materialize_blank_slot_omits_record_but_file_exists checks that an all-blank run yields {"tokens": []} but never loads that empty file via _load_static_tokens / StaticBearerVerifier, so the change's declared 'fails-closed at startup ("defines no tokens")' behavior for the named input {"tokens": []} is untested.
scenarios: An operator seeds no PATs; a regression that makes _load_static_tokens tolerate an empty token set (or StaticBearerVerifier construct anyway) would leave MCP open instead of fail-closed, and no test would catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the all-blank branch of test_materialize_blank_slot_omits_record_but_file_exists (or a new test), assert pytest.raises(AuthConfigError) when calling _load_static_tokens(str(tokens_file2)) / constructing StaticBearerVerifier over the empty tokens file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the prose-substring runbook assertions with either a structural check of a canonical, consumer-read identifier, or drop the test as a change-detector.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mcp_client_pats.py: 'assert "rotat" in text', 'assert "restart" in text or "replace" in text or "blue-green" in text', 'assert "autodeploy" in text', 'assert "value-only" in text or "value only" in text'

The grepped tokens are prose words in infra/runbooks/mcp-client-pats.md; no CI runner, parser, or registry branches on them — an LLM/human is the only consumer (Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not cover prose-wording greps).
Rule 4 litmus: rewording the runbook (e.g. 'operator-driven token rotation' → 'manual rotation by the operator') preserves all documented behavior yet breaks 'rotat'/'restart' assertions.
advisory.finding: test_runbook_documents_operator_driven_rotation asserts the presence of prose wording substrings ('rotat', 'restart'/'replace'/'blue-green', 'autodeploy', 'value-only') in a human-readable .md runbook. These tokens are not canonical identifiers consumed by any non-human parser/validator; the assertions guard the author's phrasing and would break on a behavior-preserving reword, making this a change-detector rather than a behavior verifier.
scenarios: A doc rewrite that keeps the same operational guidance but changes wording fails this test with no behavior change.
advisory.suggested_fix: If runbook existence/section presence must be enforced, assert on a stable canonical heading/anchor rather than free-text words; otherwise remove the wording assertions.
